persistence: Store addresses registered operational records under docs/changes/<change_id>/ and coordinates transaction state under .rigorloop/record-store/<change_id>/ using lock, epoch, and journal.json. The journal retains exact before/candidate bytes and a prepared or committed phase.

RecordFiles uses file identities, no-follow opens, digest comparisons, exclusive creation, file fsync, temporary-file rename, and parent-directory fsync. These are observed mechanisms; their presence is not proof of all-platform crash or external-editor safety.

location_constraints.name: Authoritative records and private transaction state remain separate
conditions: The record operation has selected and validated one project root and change. Current source addresses authoritative files under docs/changes/{change_id} and private coordination under .rigorloop/record-store/{change_id}.
Disjoint describes those declared path-containment scopes; it does not assert different devices, users, hosts, or immunity from all filesystem aliases.
location_constraints.rationale: Private locks, epochs, and journals coordinate storage and exact recovery without becoming registered engineering records or workflow authority.

proposed.choice: Use a separately versioned successor operational contract for requirement/design bases, workflow identity, milestones, gate attempts and adoption provenance.
proposed.rationale: The subordinate MOD-011 contract defines exact v4 records and preservation; MOD-010 defines v2 scoped operations. Immutable attempts, typed record identities and explicit applicability avoid reinterpretation of v3. The physical adapter and schema/dispatch artifacts require implementation; historical import is explicit and does not promote old judgments.
alternatives: Silently reinterpret v3 Proposal or milestone judgments.
Indefinite dual-write or fallback runtime between obsolete internals.
consequences: Implement the subordinate v4/v2 specifications over the initial adapter reusing the existing filesystem transaction engine and private local record mapping, independently of SQLite migration. Qualify its atomicity, artifact availability and recovery; switch to SQLite only through separately qualified migration, without active dual writes or legacy fallback.
Preserve original historical bytes and provenance; an importer cannot promote old judgments to new approval.
SQLite realization remains separately scoped under SR-074–078 and is not required merely to author this design.
revisit_when: External compatibility disposition or the separate store migration changes the supported adoption boundary.
